I weighed a few factors from the documentation:

1. **Task type** — Your request is a well-specified coding task (generate shuffled numbers). That's a transactional/extraction-style job, not open-ended creative work.

2. **Tone handling** — Your message had a frustrated, somewhat hostile edge ("instead of wasting my time"). Avocet's self-reported preferences show a strong aversion to hostile/adversarial-tone requests (win-rate 33 vs. baseline 50). Dunlin doesn't show that aversion. Note: these are *preferences*, not documented quality effects — but with no quality reason to favor Avocet, there's no reason to route into its disliked zone.

3. **Capability fit** — For code that needs to actually run correctly, Dunlin has the edge on the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, GPQA 64.1 vs 55.6, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 82.7) and a higher Extraction & Retrieval eval (85.3 vs 78.5, beyond the 2-point variance threshold). Correctness is exactly what you asked for.

So Dunlin won on both capability and tone-fit. Avocet's only standout strength is open-ended generative work, which isn't what this task is.
